aspect: The claim is a second job
description: Photographs, statements, medical records, assessor appointments, adjuster calls, courtesy car arrangements - all handled by the person who is injured and has no car.
energy_note: Administered by whoever is least able to.

description: Both insurers act for their own client. A dispute over who was at fault can run for months while the repair waits.
energy_note: Your account of what happened, treated as a bid.

aspect: The premium goes up either way
description: A claim raises the renewal price whether or not the fault was yours, and the increase persists for years.
energy_note: Paying for years for four seconds.

description: Hit at 20 km/h at a junction. Barely any visible damage. Six weeks later the neck pain has not gone, physio is capped at eight sessions, and the other insurer has disputed liability.
energy_note: A minor accident that reorganises a year.

aspect: No car is its own problem
description: Until the repair or payout, getting to work, school and the shops becomes a daily logistics exercise with a cost attached.
He looked at his phone. Nobody was hurt. He still has the excess, the no-claims loss, the repair wait and the small private fact of having done it.
energy_note: The same paperwork, plus the part you cannot tell anyone.
